title: A table, a cubic and an inverse

stimulus.title: Values of $f$, and the function $g$
stimulus.text: The table gives values of the function $f$ at selected inputs. The function $g$ is defined by $g(x) = 0.5x^3 - 2x + 1$ for every real number $x$.

table.caption: Values of the function f at x = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Find the value of $f(g(2))$, or indicate that it cannot be found from the information given. Show the work that leads to your answer.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Find every value of $x$ in the table for which $f(x) = 2$.

rubric.point: Both $x = -1$ and $x = 3$, and no other value

parts.sample: From the table, $f(-1) = 2$ and $f(3) = 2$, so $x = -1$ and $x = 3$.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Find every value of $x$ for which $g(x) = 2$. Give each answer correct to three decimal places.

rubric.point: All three solutions, each correct to three decimal places
accept: values that round or truncate to these three

parts.sample: Graph $y = 0.5x^3 - 2x + 1$ and $y = 2$ on a window such as $-4 \le x \le 4$; they meet three times: $x \approx -1.675$ and $x \approx -0.539$ and $x \approx 2.214$.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Write the end behavior of $g$ as $x$ decreases without bound, using limit notation.
parts.sample: The leading term $0.5x^3$ is negative and grows without bound in size as $x$ decreases, so $\lim_{x \to -\infty} g(x) = -\infty$.

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: Is $f$ invertible? Give a reason for your answer using values from the table.

rubric.point: No, with two specific inputs that share an output
accept: No: the inputs $-1$ and $3$ both give the output $2$

parts.sample: No. $f(-1) = 2$ and $f(3) = 2$: two different inputs give the same output, so $f$ has no inverse.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: Is $g$ invertible on the set of real numbers? Give a reason for your answer using specific values of $g$.

rubric.point: No, with two specific inputs of $g$ that share an output
accept: No, because $g$ takes the value $2$ at three inputs (part B(i))

parts.sample: No. $g(0) = 1$ and $g(2) = 0.5(8) - 4 + 1 = 1$, so two different inputs give the same output and $g$ has no inverse on the real numbers.
